section: Art, architecture and archaeology in Andhra Pradesh after 1956; museums and heritage

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Sri Panakala Narasimha Swamy Temple at Mangalagiri is correct?
o: The Archaeological Survey of India has begun scientific conservation of the temple, which includes a 16th-century mandapam and a 19th-century 153-foot gopuram.
The Archaeological Survey of India has begun cosmetic restoration of a 16th-century gopuram and a 19th-century mandapam at the temple.
The temple has a 15th-century mandapam and an 18th-century 135-foot gopuram under conservation by the Archaeological Survey of India.
The temple's conservation concerns only its 19th-century mandapam and does not include the gopuram.
accepted.x: The Archaeological Survey of India began scientific conservation of the Sri Panakala Narasimha Swamy Temple at Mangalagiri. The temple complex includes a 16th-century mandapam and a 19th-century gopuram measuring 153 feet.
accepted.tq: Use the precise combination of institution, conservation method, dates and measurements.

accepted.s: The Tourism Department's “Discover Andhra” campaign promotes a Buddhist heritage circuit comprising which of the following sites?
o: Amaravati, Thotlakonda and the Sri Panakala Narasimha Swamy Temple
accepted.x: The “Discover Andhra” campaign promotes a Buddhist heritage circuit comprising Amaravati, Bavikonda and Thotlakonda.
accepted.tq: Test the complete named list by identifying the option without a non-Buddhist site.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was identified as an unfinished item of the 2014 bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Reconstruction of the 153-foot gopuram at Mangalagiri
Transfer of all temple conservation functions to the Archaeological Survey of India
accepted.x: The division of museum antiques remained one of the unfinished items arising from the 2014 bifurcation.
accepted.tq: Apply the institutional consequence to the specific unresolved bifurcation issue.

accepted.s: A heritage site has been given a superficial facelift without proper study of its historical fabric or the likely effects of surrounding development. Which approach best addresses the criticism involved?
o: Scientific conservation along with heritage impact assessment
Promotion of the site only through tourism campaigns
Replacement of all old structures with modern replicas
accepted.x: Cosmetic restoration is criticised for failing to protect the authentic historical character of heritage sites. Scientific conservation and heritage impact assessment provide the appropriate corrective approach.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the criticised cosmetic approach from the conservation-based solution in an applied situation.
